finalText:
Redis died at 2:14am and never came back. `10.0.0.12:6379` refused every reconnect try, all the way to attempt 12 at 2:31am.

Losing redis pushed every request onto direct store reads. That triggered cache miss storms and 5-second timeouts across `api`, `worker-1`, `worker-2`, and `scheduler`, all at once.

The request queue should have capped at 500. It didn't. It climbed past 568 while the timeouts kept piling up behind it.

By 2:31:44am `worker-2` ran out of memory from the backlog and crashed. Eight seconds later the supervisor gave up and killed the whole service.

Fix redis first, then put a real cap on that queue so one dead dependency can't take the whole thing down again.
